findings.title: Hardcoded secret in source code
findings.explanation: A sensitive API token has been hardcoded directly into the source code, violating security best practices.
findings.suggestion: Load the API token from environment configuration using config() or env() instead.

findings.title: Inefficient database query and collection filtering
findings.explanation: Calling User::all() loads all records into memory before filtering them in PHP. This is a performance anti-pattern and can cause memory issues as the users table grows.
findings.suggestion: Use Eloquent query scopes or database where clauses like User::where('name', 'like', '%' . $term . '%')->get(); instead.

findings.title: Use strict comparison for strpos
findings.explanation: Using loose comparison '==' with strpos can lead to bugs if '/admin' is found at index 0, since 0 evaluates to false in loose comparisons.

findings.title: N+1 query problem inside loop
findings.explanation: Accessing $order->customer inside a loop results in an N+1 query problem, running a separate database query for each order.
findings.suggestion: Use eager loading like Order::with('customer')->latest()->take(50)->get() and pluck the customer names.

findings.title: Unescaped output on user-controlled data
findings.explanation: Using {!! !!} in Blade renders raw HTML, which can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities if the comment body contains unescaped user input.
findings.suggestion: Use {{ $comment->body }} instead to automatically escape output.

findings.title: Potential ZeroDivisionError
findings.explanation: Dividing by visits without checking if visits is zero can raise an unhandled ZeroDivisionError when visits equals 0.
findings.suggestion: Check if visits is zero before performing the division, or handle the exception appropriately.

findings.title: Avoid using eval on external input
findings.explanation: Using eval() on user-controlled input allows arbitrary code execution and is a severe security vulnerability.
findings.suggestion: Replace eval() with a safe math expression parser or library.

findings.title: Mutable default argument used
findings.explanation: Using a mutable object like a list as a default argument in Python causes shared state across function calls.
findings.suggestion: Use None as the default value and instantiate a new list inside the function if the argument is None.

findings.title: SQL Injection vulnerability
findings.explanation: Building SQL queries by formatting variables directly into the query string allows SQL injection attacks.
findings.suggestion: Use parameterized queries like conn.execute("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", (name,))

findings.title: Bare or empty except block swallows exceptions
findings.explanation: Swallowing all exceptions silently with 'pass' makes debugging difficult and hides unexpected errors like FileNotFoundError vs JSONDecodeError or permission errors.
findings.suggestion: Catch specific exceptions such as FileNotFoundError or log the exception before returning the default dict.
